 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 Amira Elghawaby applied for a waiver of the one-year limitation period that applies to former reporting public office holders following the end of their term of office. The waiver of the limitation period allows Amira Elghawaby to accept an offer of employment from TMFoundation.
In reviewing Amira Elghawaby’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which includes the following: 
The circumstances under which the reporting public office holder left her office:
The Government of Canada terminated the role of the Special Representative on Combatting Islamophobia in order to replace it with a new Advisory Council on Rights, Equality and Inclusion. One year remained in the mandate of the Special Representative on Combatting Islamophobia.
The general employment prospects of the former reporting public office holder: 
Given Ms. Elghawaby’s specialized skillset and expertise, finding employment could take longer than anticipated. This is because Ms. Elghawaby’s mandate concluded with little notice, and she had wide engagement with organizations serving Muslim communities throughout her tenure, including in the past year.
The nature, and significance to the Government of Canada, of information possessed by the former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office: 
The Special Representative's mandate was primarily to advise the Government of Canada on the experiences of Canadian Muslims, provide policy guidance, offer training, raise general awareness about Islamophobia, and help reframe narratives. The work was publicly communicated through an Annual Report and regular social media postings, and as such, already largely part of the public realm.
The facilitation of interchange between the private and public sector:
The role focused on creating understanding between public officials and communities regarding Islamophobia's impact on various aspects of Canadian life. 
That engagement was important to help facilitate understanding and appreciation for the specific challenges faced by Canadian Muslims in exercising their freedom of religion, freedom of expression, and other human rights. 
The degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage by hiring the former reporting public office holder: 
Because the TMFoundation is a charity, its work has no commercial aspect. 
The authority and influence possessed by the former reporting public office holder while in public office:
The Special Representative's authority and influence was related only to fulfilling the mandate to serve as a "champion, advisor, expert, and representative to the Canadian government, for the purpose of enhancing efforts to combat Islamophobia and to promote awareness of the diverse and intersectional identities of Muslims in Canada".
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the waiver in relation the acceptance of an offer of employment of TMFoundation outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore agreed to waive the limitation period for this offer of employment. 
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making any other representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the remainder of Amira Elghawaby’s limitation period.
